assessment: This work focuses on the important problem of how a human pathogenic fungus obtains iron during infection. This study uses biochemical and genetic methods to identify the missing link between heme receptors and heme utilization by cells. Specifically, they provide convincing evidence that the ferric reductase-like proteins Frp1 and Frp2 have major roles in iron acquisition from heme, thus identifying a new function for these proteins. Understanding how pathogenic fungi obtain iron and identifying differences in fungal and host iron metabolism can provide valuable leads for drug discovery.
